paper.title_en: Coherent and Dissociative Photon-Induced Production in Herwig 7
paper.abstract_en:
We present a particle-level study of photon-induced production in Herwig~7, focusing on coherent, single-dissociative, and double-dissociative proton configurations. The simulation combines the Budnev elastic photon flux with an inelastic photon PDF, using the internal Herwig~7 matrix elements for $\gamma\gamma \to \ell^+\ell^-$ and $\gamma\gamma \to W^+W^- \to \ell^+\ell^-\nu\bar{\nu}$ as the central setup. Using a dedicated Rivet analysis, we compare hard-system kinematics, charged-particle activity, rapidity-gap observables, and distributions sensitive to forward proton remnants.

We find that variations in shower settings generally have modest effects on hard-system distributions in well-populated phase-space regions, whereas coherent and dissociative samples exhibit more pronounced differences in additional charged-particle activity and rapidity-gap observables. These results provide a useful baseline for modelling semi-exclusive photon-induced measurements at the LHC and identify observables that are particularly sensitive to dissociative activity in future Monte Carlo generator comparisons.
